lines.trans: Lending is out of the question, but I'll gladly buy something off you in cash.
This pebble right here—how would you sell it?
This stone traveled across the oceans of the world to finally reach this beach—a one-of-a-kind stone in all the world!
Tossed by rough waves and licked smooth millions of times into this lovely form—isn't it remarkably sexy?
Simply put, it is the Earth—a tiny Earth! Wouldn't you like to feel its hidden power in your own hand?

words.gram: Auxiliary na-adjective expressing appearance or likeness.

lines.trans: May I? Ah, it really does fit.
Just as the glass slipper fit snugly onto Cinderella's foot, this stone fits right into your palm!
Mr. Kawada, I wasn't the one who handed it to you—it was the stone's own will!
And I tripped over my tongue right at the punchline!
Today the Earth itself is running a special promotion for us! Magnificent!

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.

examples.text: お前が貸せ。ヤクザから巻き上げた金があるだろ、バラすぞ。

meanings.note: Polite/dialectal negative ending, especially in ～ません.
Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.
Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).

meanings.en: do a favor for the speaker
meanings.note: After a te-form (会ってくれる？), warmly asks 'will you do that for us?'

examples.trans: Will you come again for me?

examples.text: 母が料理を作ってくれました。
examples.trans: My mother cooked food for me.

meanings.note: Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.

meanings.en: to think; to feel; to believe
meanings.note: Often follows quotative と to express an opinion or belief.

examples.text: それはいいと思います。

meanings.note: Loanword from English 'salesman'.

examples.text: 彼は優秀なセールスマンです。

examples.trans: I want to become a full-fledged salesman.

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.
Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
First-person pronoun commonly used by men and boys in friendly or polite everyday settings.

examples.text: 僕もコーヒーをください。

meanings.note: Read なん before だ/です/の, and なに before が/を or alone.

examples.text: 何を買いにきましたか。

meanings.note: Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.
て-form 売って links 'sell' into the next action.
Follows a verb's て-form or polite お + stem (お待ちください, お持ち帰りください) to make a polite request.

examples.text: ここに書いてください。

meanings.en: whichever (after question word); or something like
meanings.note: After どれ (どれでも) means 'any one at all'; after a noun (店でも) suggests an example ('a shop or something').

examples.text: いつでも来てください。

meanings.note: Attaches to quantities or interrogatives (どのぐらい, 何本ぐらい) to indicate approximation.
